newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SCARRED CENTRE COURT UNDER THE MICROSCOPE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SCARRED CENTRE COURT UNDER THE MICROSCOPE.

text.p: The worn state of Wimbledon's normally flawless Centre Court has forced the All England Club to take action to safeguard the surface for the final stages of the championships.
Players and spectators have been taken aback by ruts which have appeared in mid-court on both sides of the net, and even head groundsman Eddie Seaward admits he is "concerned" about the situation.

"I am obviously concerned about the condition of Centre Court, but we are increasing the air flow through the night with the use of fans and, once the moisture has dried out, I am confident the court will become firmer, look better and continue to perform well."

Wimbledon officials blame the damage on the wet weather which forced the court to be covered much earlier than normal before the championships, and "sweating" under the covers during the soggy first week.
Jana Novotna and Pete Sampras are among those who feel the resultant surface is becoming an issue.

"I must say that the Centre Court is really badly damaged," said Novotna. "It changes the whole game. On the outside courts you can approach anywhere you want, but on Centre Court you have to approach absolutely through the middle, because there is a path where you never get a decent bounce."
Sampras was equally surprised. "I couldn't believe it in the warm-up....in the middle of the court there was no grass," the American reported. "I've never seen Centre Court so chopped up."
An All England Club spokesman insisted there was no prospect of the Centre Court being taken out of service.
